Note · S&P Global's mission and the forces on it — the slogan changed three times; the business underneath never did. Volatility and refinancing are fuel, and the 2026 danger is LLM front ends and venue-owned prices turning the data layer into a commodity

Strategy / environment-scan note · Maps to Course 04 (Competitive Strategy: five forces, coopetition, platform power), Course 11 (Global Strategy & Macro: China ratings, Russia exit, tariffs, Middle East energy shock), E5 (Transformation: conglomerate → "operating company" → four-division data firm), E6 (Crisis Leadership: COVID, the 2022 issuance collapse, 2025 tariffs), E9 (Geopolitics & Macro), E10 (Digital & AI Transformation) · Written 2026-10-25 · Part of spglobal hub; companions spglobal esg reversal, spglobal strategy financials, spglobal ai data layer

  • Source: the S&P Global corpus at _ingest/raw/spglobal/ (492 full texts, 2019-01-01 → 2026-10-23). It includes 476 press and IR releases, the CEO and chairman letters for 2019–2025, and the Investor Day decks of Dec 2022 and Nov 2025. "About S&P Global" boilerplate was traced phrase by phrase, with first and last dates (§1b). Every line here is S&P's own text or text it chose to publish, so the note reads it for what it reveals and what it leaves out. Earnings releases after Q1 2023 are stubs in the corpus, so yearly figures come from the letters and decks (see _ingest/raw/spglobal/DIGEST.md §1).
  • Core claim: S&P Global rewrote its slogan three times in seven years:
  • "Powering the Markets of the Future" (2018–2021), with the purpose line Accelerating Progress.
  • "Powering Global Markets" and Accelerate Progress (Dec 2022 – 2024).
  • "Advancing Essential Intelligence" (Nov 2025 →).

The business did not change. S&P sells proprietary benchmarks, ratings and data that regulated workflows must use: in 2025 it said these make up "over 95 percent of our revenue". Volatility and refinancing waves are fuel, not threats: 2020 was a record year, and the 2026–28 "maturity wall" is a selling point. Two things changed: what kind of company S&P says it is, and what threatens it. - Identity: the story moved from a conglomerate of four divisions, to a scale merger with IHS Markit, to a narrower firm that sells off non-core lines. - Threat: in 2019 the risk was cyclical, meaning Ratings issuance. By 2026 it is structural. AI front ends (Claude, Copilot, Gemini) now sit between S&P and the user. A trading venue's prices (MarketAxess CP+, soon to be ICE's) feed S&P's own bond evaluations. Both push S&P's data toward commodity status. S&P admits the cyclical risks and lists generative AI as a competitive risk. It never discusses fee pressure on its own products, the CP+ dependency after ICE's bid for MarketAxess, or its Ratings franchise's conflicts.

1. Mission and identity

1a. What S&P says it is for (verbatim, dated)

Date Speaker / item Line (verbatim) Read
2019 (AR, pub. Mar 2020) Peterson, CEO letter purpose "we express as Accelerating Progress in the World"; strategy is the "mission statement we call Powering the Markets of the Future" Purpose is why, strategy is how. Both are written to be broad
2020-07-28 Peterson, Q2 results "The need for our products has increased during these uncertain times" Crisis demand is part of the identity
2021-04-26 Corporate boilerplate "We've been providing essential intelligence that unlocks opportunity, fosters growth and accelerates progress for more than 160 years." Essential intelligence starts as a phrase in the boilerplate
2021 (AR, pub. Mar 2022) Peterson, "The Next Era of Essential Intelligence" "Essential intelligence is the powerful combination of the right data, technologies and people that enables our customers to make decisions with conviction." The concept is defined, in the year of the merger
2022-12-01 Investor Day "By Powering Global Markets, We Accelerate Progress" The post-merger reset: vision and purpose in one line
2022 (AR, pub. Mar 2023) Peterson "Powering Global Markets is our vision and a strategic framework we use to allocate capital, channel innovation, inspire our people" The slogan doubles as the capital-allocation framework
2023-05-23 O'Hanlon, Chief Corporate Responsibility & Diversity Officer "Our company's purpose – to accelerate progress – underpins the work we do for our people, customers and communities" Purpose kept alive by the corporate-responsibility function
2025-03-25 Livingston, incoming Chairman "S&P Global's mission to provide Essential Intelligence has never been more important." Essential Intelligence is now capitalised as a brand
2025-11-13 → 2026 Investor Day 2025; Cheung's 2025 letter mission "Advancing Essential Intelligence", with three objectives: Advancing Market Leadership, Expanding into High-growth Adjacencies, Amplifying Enterprise Capabilities and AI Cheung's first strategy of her own
2026-07-06 Cheung, MI operating model "In a world where data is abundant, but not all created equal, customers need trusted, connected, essential intelligence" The mission recast for the AI era: trusted data is the scarce good
2026-09-14 Clay, CEO S&P DJI (Kaiko stake) "our mission to advance essential intelligence by bridging traditional and decentralized finance" The mission stretched to cover DeFi

The arc: - 2019–21: power the markets of the future, plus a purpose line. - 2022–24: power global markets, accelerate progress. - 2025–26: advance essential intelligence, aimed at AI and DeFi.

The purpose line Accelerate Progress runs from the 2019 annual report to the Oct 2025 boilerplate. It is absent from the 2025 CEO and chairman letters.

1b. The "About S&P Global" boilerplate, 2019 → 2026

First seen Self-description (key words) Read
2019–21 "world's foremost provider of credit ratings, benchmarks and analytics in the global capital and commodity markets" (last seen Jun 2022) Four divisions, sold on breadth
2022-02-28 (merger close) "provides essential intelligence. We enable governments, businesses and individuals … make decisions with conviction." Adds "guiding them through ESG and energy transition across supply chains" and "global capital, commodity and automotive markets" IHS Markit adds autos (Mobility). ESG is in the second sentence
2024-07-30 ESG replaced by "sustainability and energy transition"; everything else identical (the last "ESG" version was 2024-04-25) A quiet de-ESG edit; see spglobal esg reversal
2025-04-29 → 2025-10-30 "automotive markets" still present, six months after the Mobility spin was announced The boilerplate lags strategy
2026-02-10 Rewritten: "enables businesses, governments, and individuals with trusted data … We are Advancing Essential Intelligence through world-leading benchmarks, data, and insights"; "guiding them through the energy expansion, acceleration of artificial intelligence, and evolution of public and private markets" Three new tailwinds named: energy expansion, AI, private markets. "Accelerate progress" is gone
2026-04-28 / 07-28 Small edits: "thrive economically" becomes "thrive"; "guiding them through" becomes "navigating" Housekeeping

What the boilerplate shows (inference unless noted): 1. Two verbs never reconciled: confidence vs conviction. - Corporate texts and CEO quotes have said "make decisions with conviction" since 2019 (36 items). - S&P DJI and Ratings boilerplates still say "make decisions with confidence" (60 items, last seen 2026-10-22). - After seven years and a merger, the divisions still do not speak with one brand voice. 2. The legal self-description followed strategy only after the fact. - "Automotive" stayed in until after Investor Day 2025. - "ESG" stayed until mid-2024, months after the company had begun to reposition. - Read the boilerplate as a lagging indicator. 3. It names tailwinds, not products. The 2026 text lists energy expansion, AI and private markets, the three growth stories of Investor Day 2025. Ratings, the biggest profit pool, is described only as "benchmarks".

1c. Values and culture claims

  • Values:
  • 2019: excellence, relevance, integrity.
  • 2021: rewritten as discovery, partnership, integrity, which Cheung repeats in 2024.
  • People:
  • "Putting Our People First" (AR 2019) became the People First philosophy (2023 DEI report), then People Forward (AR 2024).
  • In 2025 People Forward is tied to mandatory "AI for Everyone" training and the StepForward youth programme ($10M over three years, 2025-12-17).
  • Integrity and independence are repeated every year by S&P DJI ("As an independent index provider, we hold ourselves to the highest standards of integrity and transparency", Draper, 2020-08-05). The same index business paid a $9M SEC penalty in May 2021 (spglobal indices benchmarks).
  • Purpose as an executive role, then not: a Chief Purpose Officer sat on the 2022 Investor Day executive committee. The role ended in the Oct 2024 leadership reshuffle, and corporate-responsibility disclosures moved under the CFO.

1d. What S&P actually optimises for (inference, judged by actions)

Stated Revealed by action Evidence
"Powering the Markets of the Future" (breadth) Scale first, then subtract The $44B IHS Markit merger (2020). Within four years it sold or spun off Engineering Solutions ($975M), Fincentric, PrimeOne, OSTTRA ($3.1B, split with CME), Mobility and EDM/thinkFolio, plus the forced remedies (spglobal ihs markit merger)
"Essential intelligence" Own the must-use standard: ratings, indices, identifiers, benchmarks CUSIP was given up only under an EC remedy. LoanX IDs were extended to private credit (2025). Capital IQ IDs were published free on DUNL.org (2025): lock-in through the identifier
"Advancing Market Leadership" Margin and capital return Adjusted operating margin 44.9% (2022) → 50.4% (2025). Since 2022, 145% of adjusted FCF returned vs an "at least 85%" framework (Investor Day 2025). Cheung on the July 2026 reorganisation: "growing our revenue and improving margins"
"Amplifying … AI" Distribution through others' front ends Kensho LLM-ready API (2024); MCP into Claude (2025), AWS, Google, Microsoft, Cohere (2026) (spglobal ai data layer)
"Bridging traditional and decentralized finance" License the brand onto new venues; keep the risk small S&P 500 perpetuals on Hyperliquid, tokenized iBoxx TRS on Canton, Kaiko stake, OpenZeppelin. All deal values undisclosed and "not material" (spglobal digital assets)

The tension (inference): the mission says essential, meaning customers cannot do without it. The 2026 actions say distribute everywhere. Those fit together only while S&P's data is the standard that every LLM and venue must license. If an AI front end or a venue (CP+, Tradeweb's Ai-Price) can produce a good enough number, essential turns into one input among several.

2. Tailwinds

# Tailwind Evidence (dated, quantified, as S&P states) Who says
T1 Debt issuance and refinancing Q2 2020: Ratings +26%; Peterson: "Companies, particularly in the U.S., have turned to the bond market to raise liquidity during this COVID-19 pandemic". Investor Day 2025: "$8T+ corporate debt rated by S&P Global Ratings is maturing over the next 3 years" vs a $6.5T average Peterson; Investor Day 2025
T2 Passive investing and index licensing ETF AUM on S&P indices $1.7T (2019) → $2.0T (2020) → $2.8T (2021). "$27.7 trillion in assets indexed or benchmarked to all S&P Dow Jones Indices" (Investor Day 2025). Exchange-traded derivatives fees rise with volatility S&P DJI
T3 AI raises the value of trusted proprietary data "customers are placing an even higher value on S&P Global's proprietary benchmarks, data, and tools" (Cheung, AR 2025). "over $1 billion invested in AI" since Kensho (2018). 60,000+ Capital IQ Pro GenAI users (Investor Day 2025) Cheung
T4 Private markets and private credit Private-markets revenue ~$400M (2022) → $430M (2023) → $535M (2024). With Intelligence ($1.8B, 2025). Saha: "The expansion of private credit and the emergence of secondary trading necessitates common identifiers" (2025-06-24) Cheung, Saha
T5 Energy expansion and the AI build-out "The next two decades will be characterized by energy expansion, not replacement" (Cheung, AR 2025). datacenterHawk and Enertel acquired (2026). Ratings: hyperscaler capex above $1.3T by 2027 (2026-08-27) Cheung, Ernsberger
T6 Regulation that requires an independent number EU BMR endorsement (2019-03-01); IOSCO reviews yearly; SEC Rule 2a-5 fair-value diligence (PVR Source, 2022); T+1 (DTCC ALERT link, 2024); China domestic ratings licences (2019, 2020) Matturri, Draper, MI
T7 Digital assets gaining legitimacy Stablecoins $301bn vs $173bn a year earlier; GENIUS Act cited (2025-10-14). Vault deposits $1.5B → ~$10B (2024→2026) Ratings, S&P DJI
T8 Geopolitical and macro uncertainty Peterson: "The demand for our ratings, benchmarks, research, data, and analytics is greater than ever during uncertain and volatile markets" (2020-10-27) Peterson

Top three (judgement): T1 (refinancing), T2 (passive), T3 (proprietary data in an AI world). T3 is the most contested: the same tailwind is also H1 below.

3. Headwinds and challenges

A = S&P acknowledges it. I = my inference, or context the corpus omits.

# Headwind Evidence A / I
H1 LLM front ends take the customer interface S&P pushes its data into Claude, Copilot, Gemini, Cohere and Quick Suite. Investor Day 2025 lists "competitive products (including those incorporating generative artificial intelligence" as a risk. Farsight's CEO, quoted in an S&P release: "The industry has spent years competing on access to data." A for the risk factor; I that the terminal (Capital IQ Pro) loses pricing power
H2 Venue-owned prices S&P Evaluated Bond Pricing takes MarketAxess CP+ (2024-10-31). ICE agreed to buy MarketAxess (2026-07-30, per ice hub). The corpus never mentions CP+ again. Tradeweb's Ai-Price competes directly (tradeweb ai price §5) I
H3 Ratings cyclicality 2022: guidance suspended. "Debt issuance volumes have been extraordinarily weak year-to-date" (2022-06-01). Ratings hit "by as much as $600 million". Transaction revenue −56% in Q3 2022 A
H4 Regulatory and conduct cost SEC penalties: $9M (S&P DJI, 2021), $2.5M (Ratings, 2022), $20M (Ratings off-channel comms, 2024). Merger remedies forced the sales of CUSIP, LCD and OPIS A
H5 Geopolitics and tariffs "The impact of the Russia/Ukraine conflict was the most significant headwind to revenue and profit margins in the quarter" (Commodity Insights, Q2 2022). Investor Day 2025 market-forces slide: "Geopolitical and regulatory uncertainty", "Tariff disruptions" A
H6 Fee compression at the customer Investor Day 2025: "Fee compression at passive managers". The risk factors name "the impact of customer cost-cutting pressures" every year A that customers are squeezed; I that S&P's own prices follow
H7 Narrative risk: ESG ESG targets were missed ($800M by 2026 vs $359M in 2024), the "ESG" wording was dropped, and Sustainable1 was folded (spglobal esg reversal) A for the figures; I for the reading
H8 Leadership churn No permanent CFO for about a year (2024). Three MI leaders in two years. Heads of S&P DJI and Mobility replaced in 2025. A new Chief Technology & Transformation Officer and Chief Legal Officer in 2026 (spglobal people) I
H9 Upstream energy softness "Softness in upstream energy market" (Investor Day 2025); upstream software sold to SLB (2026) A
H10 Conflicts at the Ratings–data boundary Credit Analytics moved into Ratings and OpenZeppelin reports to the Ratings President (2026). Releases add "S&P Global Market Intelligence and S&P Global Ratings are separately managed divisions of S&P Global." I. The disclaimers show the company knows the issue exists

What S&P acknowledges vs leaves out: it openly discusses cyclicality, geopolitics, tariffs and "AI" as a generic risk. It does not discuss its own pricing power, its dependence on CP+ after the ICE deal, the conflict between selling ratings and selling data, or why ESG was folded.

4. Forces map, 2026 (five forces + regulation + technology)

Pressure score: 1 = benign, 5 = severe (judgement). Arrows show the change since 2019.

Force Score Trend One-line evidence
Rivalry 3 ↑ The peer group S&P names in every annual report: Moody's, CME, MSCI, FactSet, Verisk, ICE. ICE is now also a pricing rival that will own CP+. Bloomberg is both a rival and a partner (TSOX–InvestorAccess, 2023)
New entrants 2 ↑ slowly Ratings and benchmark licences (EU BMR, NRSRO, CRA rules) are high barriers. AI-native analytics firms (Farsight, Rogo) enter at the workflow layer, not the data layer
Supplier power 3 ↑ Evaluated pricing depends on dealer contributions (Barclays, 2025) and venue prices (CP+). Visible Alpha depends on bank contributors
Buyer power 3 ↑ Fee-compressed passive managers. Enterprise deals run through the Chief Client Office. Hyperscalers and LLM vendors are new distribution buyers
Substitutes 3 ↑ Model prices (Ai-Price), free identifiers (S&P itself published CIQ IDs), open-source carbon data (CDOP). Ratings have no close substitute (NRSRO oligopoly)
Regulation 2 (net tailwind) ↔ Rules that require independent numbers (BMR, IOSCO, Rule 2a-5) vs conduct penalties and merger remedies
Technology (AI / DLT) 4 (double-edged) ↑ Tailwind T3 and headwind H1 at the same time. Tokenization opens a new licensing channel (spglobal digital assets)
Complementors — ↑ CME (S&P DJI JV partner, 27% non-controlling interest), Cboe (VIX, SPX options), MSCI (GICS co-owner), AWS/Google/Microsoft/Anthropic, Kaiko

Read: S&P sits where most of the power is: must-use standards protected by regulation. The two forces getting worse, technology and suppliers, attack the same thing. They both threaten S&P's control over who computes the number and where it is consumed.

5. Crisis tests — what each one revealed

Shock What S&P said Numbers (as stated) What it revealed (inference)
COVID, Mar–Jun 2020 "With a severe global recession taking hold and credit pressure building" (CEO note, spring 2020). Guidance cut in April; buybacks paused Q2 2020: revenue +14%; Ratings $1,006M (+26%), adjusted margin 69.1%; Q3 revenue +9% The feared shock was a windfall. Central-bank support plus issuance made Ratings the crisis winner. Downside scenarios for Ratings are about issuance freezes, not credit stress
2022: rates, Russia, merger close Guidance suspended (Jun 1). "The impact of the Russia/Ukraine conflict was the most significant headwind" (Q2) Ratings transaction revenue −31% / −44% / −56% (Q1–Q3); pro forma revenue −4%; adjusted EPS guidance cut ~17% Rising rates hurt more than recession: issuance stopped. The merger thesis met the worst Ratings year of the period. Synergies kept margins up
2023: high rates, SVB MI: "especially in the current market environment with rising rates and an uptick in defaults" (2023-07-19) Q1 2023 Ratings −5%; FY2023 revenue +8% ex-divestitures (AR 2023) A recovery year. Credit-risk tools sold on the default cycle
2025 tariffs Mobility: "Tariff Winter" scenario at 10% probability (2025-02-04). Investor Day lists "Tariff disruptions" FY2025 revenue $15.3B (+8%), adjusted EPS +14% (AR 2025) The shock hit the unit being spun off (Mobility), not the core. Cheung: "we are seeing more tailwinds than headwinds"
2026 Middle East war / energy volatility Energy research "went to press amidst the evolving war in the Middle East with unprecedented volatility in energy markets" (2026-03-20) No quarterly figures in the corpus (stubs) Volatility is fuel for Platts benchmarks and exchange-traded derivatives fees. The test will show in Q3 2026 results (Oct 27)

Pattern: for S&P, volatility is a tailwind and issuance freezes are the headwind. Those are different shocks. The company is hurt most by rate shocks that close primary markets, not by crises that force borrowers to raise cash.

7. What the claims don't prove

  1. "Over 95 percent" proprietary. S&P defines the category itself. The share of revenue whose value depends on being the only source is a different and unpublished number.
  2. "More tailwinds than headwinds" (AR 2025) is a CEO's year-end framing, published in the same quarter the Investor Day risk factors added generative AI.
  3. Mission statements are not measured. No release reports progress against "Advancing Essential Intelligence". The 2022 Vitality Index (revenue from new or enhanced products: 8% → >10% → 11%) is the closest thing to a scorecard, and S&P defines it.
  4. Crisis resilience is selective. S&P publicises record crisis quarters (2020). It suspended guidance quietly (one release, 2022) and never published a "what broke" piece.

8. Canon lenses

  • Industry structure (canon porter competitive strategy): S&P's best businesses sit behind regulatory entry barriers (NRSRO, EU BMR). Section 4 shows the pressure moving to suppliers and substitutes, not to rivals.
  • Power (canon helmer 7 powers): cornered resource (the S&P 500 brand, rating history) plus switching costs (identifiers, benchmarks written into fund documents). AI threatens neither directly. It threatens the process power of the MI desktop.
  • Information goods (canon shapiro varian information rules): giving away CIQ IDs to sell linked data is classic version-and-lock-in.
  • Disruption (canon christensen innovators dilemma): model prices and LLM answers are "good enough" low-end entrants against evaluated pricing and desktop research, not against ratings.
  • Coopetition (canon brandenburger nalebuff coopetition): MSCI (GICS co-owner and index rival), Bloomberg (partner on primary bonds and desktop rival), CME (JV partner) and ICE (Brent co-governor, pricing rival and soon CP+ owner).
  • Antifragility (canon taleb antifragile): volatility helps S&P; issuance freezes hurt it. It is antifragile to noise and fragile to a closed primary market.
  • Good strategy (canon rumelt good strategy): three objectives and eight growth adjacencies make a list, not a kernel. See the Rep.

9. Practitioner counterpoint

  • For S&P: the slogans change, but the moat is real and visible outside S&P's own releases. Ratings is a regulated oligopoly. The S&P 500 is in ETF prospectuses. iBoxx and CDX/iTraxx are written into derivatives contracts. None of that depends on a tagline.
  • Against: the businesses that grew fastest after the merger (Mobility, Engineering Solutions, OSTTRA) are the ones it sold. The core that remains is mature. Growth now has to come from AI distribution and private markets, where S&P is a buyer of assets (With Intelligence at $1.8B for ~$130M of revenue), not the incumbent.

10. Open questions to track

  1. Does the 2026 annual report keep "Advancing Essential Intelligence" and drop Accelerate Progress for good?
  2. Will S&P DJI and Ratings boilerplates switch from "confidence" to "conviction"?
  3. Q3 2026 results (Oct 27): did the March energy shock lift Energy and S&P DJI derivatives fees?
  4. ICE–MarketAxess close (H1 2027): what happens to CP+ inside S&P Evaluated Bond Pricing?
  5. Does S&P ever disclose AI Data Portal or MCP revenue?

Rep

(a) Price the cycle. In June 2022 S&P said Ratings revenue could fall "by as much as $600 million" against guidance. FY2021 Ratings revenue was $4.10B with a 64.2% adjusted margin. Assume the lost revenue falls through at the incremental margin of ~80% (costs are mostly analysts' salaries). What is the operating-profit hit, and what share of FY2021 Ratings operating profit is it? (Answer: $600M × 0.8 = $480M. FY2021 Ratings adjusted operating profit ≈ $4.10B × 0.642 ≈ $2.63B, so the hit is ~18%.) Compare with what actually happened: transaction revenue fell 31% / 44% / 56% in Q1–Q3 2022.

(b) The refinancing wall. Investor Day 2025 shows $8.2T of S&P-rated corporate debt maturing over three years vs a $6.5T historical average. If S&P earns the same fee per dollar refinanced, by how much does the wall lift that slice of transaction revenue over the three years? (Answer: 8.2 / 6.5 − 1 ≈ +26%, the figure S&P prints.) Name two reasons the real lift will be smaller: refinancing in private credit, which S&P may not rate, and fee caps or frequent-issuer discounts.

(c) Rumelt's kernel for S&P 2027, in ≤120 words. Diagnosis: AI and venues can now produce numbers that used to require S&P; the moat is the regulated, must-cite standard, not the desktop. Guiding policy: be the cited source inside every model and venue, paid per use; stop defending the screen. Write three coherent actions, then score each against H1, H2 and H10. Hint: putting RatingsXpress into LLMs helps H1 but worsens H10.
